commits.message:
docs: delete the logging page, which documented a class that does not exist (rich-docs-site-13t.1) (#81)

`docs/logging.md` taught `RichHandler` across five runnable snippets and shipped
in the sidebar under "Integrations". `RichHandler` appears nowhere in `src/`,
`test/`, or `examples/` — a reader copying any snippet on the page got a
module-resolution error, with nothing on the page warning them.

Deleted rather than implemented, deliberately. A doc page and its code are not
peers to be reconciled: the code is the source of truth and the page is a claim
about it. Building `RichHandler` to make the page true would let an unvalidated
document set the roadmap and commit the project to a logging subsystem on the
authority of prose. If a logging integration is wanted, it gets filed on its own
merits.

Removes the page, its sidebar entry, and the `logging` term from the Guide nav
`activeMatch` regex — the hand-maintained list that would otherwise keep matching
a route that no longer resolves. No other file in the repo referenced the page or
the class.

docs:build clean (the dead-link gate), lint clean.
